sections.sectionSummaryBrief: We ask G-d to treat us like Yosef treated his brothers, providing sustenance, forgiving without resentment, and awakening repentance without suffering.

translations.translation: And this is, "Who would give you as a brother to me,"
in the manner that Yosef acted toward his brothers,
for there are several aspects in this.
For just as Yosef sustained his brothers and their children,
and also gave them a possession in the best of the land,
so too we ask from the Holy One, blessed be He, that even though we have sinned before Him, nevertheless He should give us all good.
And just as Yosef had no grudge in his heart against his brothers for having sold him into slavery
[for in addition to the fact that in practice he repaid them with good,
also in his heart he had no grudge against them],
and on the contrary, he endeavored that their sin be atoned,
[as explained above
(section 4)
that his causing them distress was in order that through this their sin would be purged],
so too we ask from the Holy One, blessed be He, that He forgive us all our sins.
For the atonement of the sin of the sale of Yosef came about through their having suffered,
and we ask that the Holy One, blessed be He, forgive us our sins not through suffering.
And as the Tzemach Tzedek said,
that the Holy One, blessed be He, is all-powerful to forgive without suffering.
And it is in the manner of what our sages, of blessed memory, said,
that they asked the Holy One, blessed be He, and He said, "Let him repent and it will be atoned for him."
For from the perspective of the Holy One, blessed be He, Who is above the chain of descent, it is possible to have atonement without suffering
(and even without a sacrifice),
but only through repentance alone.
And just as Yosef endeavored that they repent
[for one of the reasons he distressed them was in order that they repent,
for after he distressed them they said, "But we are guilty" etc.],
so too we ask from the Holy One, blessed be He, that He awaken us to return to Him
[and that the awakening to repentance be not through suffering].
And just as Yosef comforted his brothers and said to them, "Do not be distressed etc., for you sold me here, for G-d sent me before you to preserve life,"
informing and revealing to them the inner intention in their having sold him to Egypt,
that not only is this not contrary to the supernal will, but on the contrary, it was the supernal will in order that through this the exile be eased
(as above, section 5),
so too we ask from the Holy One, blessed be He,
that not only should He forgive us our sins, but beyond this, that it be revealed that the inner intention of the sins is the advantage of repentance,
and through the revelation of the intention and purpose of the sins,
they are transformed into merits.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: Although repentance is higher than the service of the righteous, the purpose of a dwelling place in the lower worlds is specifically fulfilled through the service of the righteous, as seen in the Temple being in Binyamin's portion.

translations.translation: And behold, even though in general the service of repentance is more elevated than the service of Torah and mitzvos,
for therefore, "In the place where penitents stand, even the completely righteous cannot stand,"
nevertheless, the intention of a dwelling place in the lower worlds is specifically completed through the service of the righteous.
And this is what our sages, of blessed memory, said,
that the reason the Holy Temple was specifically in the portion of Binyamin is because Binyamin was not involved in the sale of Yosef,
for at first glance it is not understood,
for behold, the tribes repented for having sold Yosef,
and in the place where penitents stand, even the completely righteous cannot stand,
so why was the Holy Temple built specifically in the portion of Binyamin?
And it is explained in Chassidus,
that the advantage of penitents over the righteous is that through repentance they reach a higher level,
but in order for there to be a drawing down of the revelation of G-dliness below,
a dwelling place in the lower worlds,
it is through the service of the righteous.
And since the Holy Temple is a matter of a dwelling place in the lower worlds,
therefore it was in the portion of Binyamin.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: The advantage of penitents is the conquest of the evil inclination (itkafya), while the advantage of the righteous is the transformation of the evil inclination (it'hapcha), and only through transformation does the lower world become a vessel for G-dly revelation.

translations.translation: And the explanation is,
that the advantage of penitents over the righteous is that they conquer their evil inclination,
the level of itkafya (subjugation),
and the advantage of the righteous is that they transform their evil inclination,
the level of it'hapcha (transformation).
And among the distinctions between itkafya and it'hapcha is,
that through itkafya there is a drawing down of the Ein Sof light that is above the chain of descent
[as per the statement,
"When the sitra achra is subjugated, the glory of the Holy One, blessed be He, is elevated in all worlds,"
the drawing down of the light that is equally in all worlds,
a light that is above relation to the worlds],
but the revelation of the drawing down that comes through itkafya is in a manner that the lower being is not a vessel for it
[for from the very fact that the lower being is in a state where it must subjugate itself against its will and nature,
it is understood that it is not a vessel for the revelation of G-dliness],
and in order for the lower being to be a vessel for the revelation, it is through the service of it'hapcha.
